result:
`bun run typecheck` passes and `bun test` reports 5 pass / 0 fail (the stack traces in the output are the framework's normal exception logging for the deliberate 422/403 cases, including the pre-existing search test).

The gap was in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:99` — `destroy()` looked up the post with `findOrFail()` and went straight to `Post.delete()`, skipping the authorization step that `edit()` and `update()` both perform. `PostPolicy.delete()` in `app/Policies/PostPolicy.ts` already implemented the correct author-only rule; nothing was calling it. I added `await this.authorize('delete', [Post, post])` immediately after the lookup, mirroring the `update()` action, so a signed-in non-author now gets a 403 from `AuthorizationException` before any delete runs, guests are still handled by the `auth` middleware already wrapping the route in `routes/web.ts`, and the author's own delete is unaffected. I also added `tests/PostDestroyAuthorization.test.ts`, which resets the database, creates two users and a post, and covers all three cases — non-author refused with 403 and the post still present, guest refused and the post still present, author redirected to `/posts` with the post gone.
